Hajek linear-weighted estimate and contribution column

Source: R/variance.R
dot-lw_estimand.Rd

Computes the Hajek LW point estimate \(\hat\mu = \sum_i u_i b_i Y_i / \sum_i u_i b_i\) for one estimand and its per-unit centred contribution column \(V_i = u_i b_i (Y_i - \hat\mu)\).

Usage

.lw_estimand(b, Y, u)

Arguments

b

per-unit identification weight column.

Y

observed outcomes.

u

per-unit weights.

Value

A list with the point estimate mu, the contribution column V, and a flag ok (FALSE when the denominator is 0 or non-finite).

Details

NOTE: following the definition of \(\hat\Sigma^K\) in Section 6 of main.tex, the contribution is NOT divided by the Hajek denominator \(D = \sum_i u_i b_i\) (which converges to 1; see the estimator definition in Section 7). The point estimate itself is the properly normalised Hajek ratio. TODO: if finite-sample D departs noticeably from 1, divide V by D for a sharper variance.

Examples

set.seed(1)
Y <- rnorm(10); b <- runif(10); u <- rep(1 / 10, 10)
est <- generalClusterExp:::.lw_estimand(b, Y, u)
est$mu               # Hajek ratio sum(u * b * Y) / sum(u * b)
#> [1] -0.1037307
sum(est$V)           # centred contributions sum to 0
#> [1] -6.938894e-18
